boundaries: the invite and add HTTP bodies

notes: Invites from the group panel, the accept/decline parameter fix, and phase 1 of history on joining: the inviter's device wraps the older key versions with the invite.

instruments.evidence: f04b8f996..b66c82264. 68ca76247 (Add Members in the group panel, the invite card's error), 167151d53 (accept/decline read :invite_id; an invite carries the older key versions wrapped for the invitee and accept grants them in the join's transaction; a direct add carries them the same way), 6111950d4 and b66c82264 (review fixes). Boundaries: the invite and add HTTP bodies, the group_invite_key_copies rows, group_key_members, the retention worker, the rendered group panel.

Read the findings of every ledger that names invites or group keys: 800d8e003 (key routes closed to non-members), a848b585c (a new migration missing from the rollback lists -- it recurred here, finding 1), da9ed20de (unwrap never proven; the forget-after-rotation rule), 2fa98568a (refusals told by code, not prose -- the new refusal reuses group_key_history_not_allowed), b28df65f3 (copy size bound -- the new path reuses validGroupKeyCopy).

instruments.why: No prompt or model payload.

instruments.evidence: Rendered in the pane as DERRF earlier: the Members tab shows an Add Members button; typing seed_user lists seed_user_2 only (seed_user_1 is a member); a click shows 'Invite sent: seed_user_2'. The card's failure message is asserted by role=alert in GroupInviteCard.test.

A throwaway integration test printed the real bodies: invite without history 201; with a held v1 201; with an unheld v5 400 {code: group_key_history_not_allowed}; with a non-integer version 400 bad_request; re-invite 201 with the same id; decline 204; direct add with a bad version 400; with a held version 201 {message: Participant added}.

Same run printed the rows: after a re-invite with no history the invite's copies are gone (replace, as designed); after decline 0 copies; a refused add leaves the user not a member (the transaction rolled back); after a good add the newcomer's state shows my_copies [{1 v1-g3}] with active version 0.

The refusal code group_key_history_not_allowed is the one ShareGroupKeyHistory already sends and the client already maps. The JSON field is history on both invite and add; versions are JSON object keys decoded into map[int]string.
The invite response shape is unchanged (id, conversation_id, status, expires_at, created_at); the client reads id only in tests. The frontend does not send history yet (phase 2).

instruments.why: One rule, in checkNewcomerHistory, used by both the invite and the add.
No worker contract changed.

instruments.evidence: NewcomerHistory is decoded by gin's JSON binding (encoding/json, tag-driven); B3 proved a history body reaches the rows.

instruments.why: No untyped accessor.

instruments.evidence: The HTTP test sends history exactly as a client will: a JSON object keyed by the version as a string, the value a wrapped copy.
A held version with a real-length copy is accepted (B3).
An unheld version, an empty copy, a group that hides its history, and a non-integer version are all refused (service test and B3).
Empty history is allowed and stores nothing; a copy over the size bound is refused by validGroupKeyCopy, the same bound rotation uses.

The sibling ShareHistory path checks history visible, the version held, and the copy valid; checkNewcomerHistory checks the same three. The add now shares the invite's transaction discipline, which it lacked.
Every branch of grantNewcomerHistory is reachable: nil, ErrGroupKeyHistory (B3), and a database error.
Errors from StoreInviteHistory, GrantInviteHistory and DropInviteHistory all answer 500 and are logged; the card now shows a failed answer instead of an unhandled rejection.
GrantInviteHistory is gated on message_history_visible read at accept time, so a group that hides its history after the invite grants nothing (service test).

instruments.why: Nothing duplicated: both paths share checkNewcomerHistory.

instruments.evidence: Finding 1's shape (a list whose head must be the newest migration): grep found only the two lists in omnichat_expansion_migration_test.go. instruments.evidence: Invite + copies, accept + grant + stale mark, and add + grant + stale mark are each one transaction; B4 showed a refused add leaves no member.

Undo paths: decline drops the copies (B4); accept drops them after granting; a re-invite replaces them; an invite that only expires kept them forever (finding 2, fixed in b66c82264 by the retention run).

Both fixes controlled: inv-r1-migration-not-in-rollback-lists fails 'expected 214_message_group_key_version, actual 220_group_invite_key_copies'; inv-r1-expired-invite-keeps-keys fails 'Should be zero, but was 1 -- an expired invite keeps no keys'. cleanupExpiredGroupInviteKeyCopies is called from runAllJobs; the retention worker is constructed and started in cmd/server/main.go:542-545.
go build ./... and go vet (handlers, services, workers, integration with -tags=integration) clean; gofmt clean; tsc -b and eslint clean; the commit hooks passed on every commit.
